subject: Mathematics
objective: Show why a truncated Taylor polynomial matches a function near a point and diverges away from it.
expectedBehavior: A base curve and polynomial approximations are visible
Adding terms changes the fit
The approximation is local, not global
misconceptions: More terms always help everywhere
The Taylor polynomial equals the function globally
requiredInteraction: Change the number of terms or the center.
correctnessCriteria: At the center, f and the approximation agree to the expected order
The approximation degrades away from the center
No claim of global equality
accessibility: alt text; keyboard control; no color-only distinction

subject: Mathematics
objective: Show how a prior and a likelihood produce a posterior in a simple screening example.
expectedBehavior: Population rectangles or counts are visible
Changing prevalence changes the posterior
The base-rate effect is visible
misconceptions: A positive test means the disease is very likely
Base rate does not matter
correctnessCriteria: Posterior is consistent with the displayed counts
Low prevalence can yield many false positives
The two rates are not confused

subject: Physics
objective: Show the relationship among voltage, resistance and current in a simple series circuit.
expectedBehavior: A circuit is visible
Changing voltage or resistance changes current
The relationship V = IR is readable
misconceptions: Current is used up by a resistor
Voltage and current are the same quantity
correctnessCriteria: I changes proportionally with V at fixed R
I changes inversely with R at fixed V
Labels carry units

subject: Physics
objective: Show why observed frequency changes when a source moves relative to an observer.
learner: Knows wave frequency and wavelength qualitatively.
expectedBehavior: Wavefronts compress ahead of a moving source
Observed frequency changes
Direction matters
misconceptions: The source emits a different frequency when moving
Only loudness changes
correctnessCriteria: Compressed wavefronts ahead of motion
Observed frequency higher when approaching
No claim that the emitter changed its rest frequency

subject: Computer Science
objective: Show a partition step around a pivot and the resulting left/right parts.
expectedBehavior: Pivot is visible
Elements move to the correct side
Recursive parts are identified
misconceptions: Quicksort always divides the array in half
Partitioning sorts the whole array immediately
requiredInteraction: Choose a pivot or step the partition.
correctnessCriteria: Elements left of pivot are <= pivot and right are >= pivot
The pivot reaches its sorted position
Recursive parts exclude the pivot

subject: Computer Science
objective: Show keys hashing to buckets and a collision being resolved.
expectedBehavior: Keys map to buckets
A collision is visible
Collision resolution changes the bucket state
misconceptions: A hash function never collides
Hash tables preserve insertion order
requiredInteraction: Insert a key or change table size.
correctnessCriteria: Same key hashes consistently
Colliding keys share a bucket and are distinguishable
No false claim of sorted order

subject: Computer Science
objective: Show the frontier and tentative distances as a shortest-path search proceeds.
expectedBehavior: Frontier and visited nodes are visible
Tentative distances update
The shortest path tree grows
misconceptions: Dijkstra works with negative weights
The first path found is always shortest
requiredInteraction: Step the algorithm or change the source.
correctnessCriteria: A node is finalized at its shortest tentative distance
Relaxation updates only when smaller
Negative weights are not used

subject: Economics
objective: Show total utility and diminishing marginal utility as consumption increases.
expectedBehavior: Total and marginal series are distinguished
Extra utility per unit falls
A decision threshold can be discussed
misconceptions: Total utility falls when marginal utility falls
Marginal utility is the total
correctnessCriteria: Marginal is the change in total
Diminishing marginal utility is visible
No claim that total must fall

subject: Statistics
objective: Show a null distribution, an observed statistic and a p-value tail without conflating it with the probability the null is true.
expectedBehavior: Null distribution and observed statistic are visible
Tail area is shown
A decision threshold is distinct from p
misconceptions: p is the probability the null is true
A small p proves the alternative
requiredInteraction: Change the observed statistic or alpha.
correctnessCriteria: Tail area matches the displayed statistic
alpha is a decision rule, not a posterior
No causal claim

subject: Chemistry
objective: Show how a concentration or temperature change shifts a reversible equilibrium.
expectedBehavior: Forward and reverse rates are visible
A disturbance changes the balance point
A new equilibrium is reached
misconceptions: The equilibrium constant changes with concentration
The reaction stops at equilibrium
correctnessCriteria: Concentration changes shift the balance without changing K (temperature fixed)
Temperature change can change K
Rates balance at equilibrium
